content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem, tracing the causal chain from the account page failures back to the ZeroDivisionError thrown at spend_summary.py:47, grounding each step in the evidence from G5309, Gbac1, and AL1.

Tracking down why: the monthly-spend feature flipped on at the time matching P1 and G971b/Gce95/G7e5d, while ruling out deploys since T9/T10 show all replicas converged on one unchanged revision. I'm also ruling out P2 since it occurred after the onset of errors (20:52:32 vs 20:47), confirmed by reverting the monthly-spend flag alone restoring health per T20/T21.

Finally, I'm pinning down the root cause: the new code path divides by the count of items purchased this month, which is zero for shoppers with no purchases, per F1.

Since G5309 shows the ZeroDivisionError at exactly F1's line number with no other supporting data rows, I'm marking this as reaching an unrun-reading-based cause. Now I need to think about how to phrase line numbers without using bare figures, and I'm starting to consider contributing factors — like whether the flag rollout happened all at once rather than staged, based on the off/on split in G971b.

For CF-3: nobody was paged — the alert wasn't linked to any on-call incident. Argus still mitigated quickly on its own, so paging likely wouldn't have shortened things, but it's still worth flagging as a standalone finding rather than a true contributing factor, maybe listed under went_wrong instead.

Another gap: the Investigator's change read never surfaced the flag change (P2) — that only showed up via Argus's own read of the flag provider. That's its own went_wrong item, pointing to an action item to make the change query also pull flag provider changes, with no direct answer link needed.

On detection timing, the alert fired after the configured rule wait following onset — I shouldn't comment on alert speed in the lessons. The flag was flipped on in production by an admin, and the real issue isn't the person but that the system allowed it without gradual rollout or an error-rate guard — that's CF-2. On the positive side, Argus did revert the flag quickly after the alert.

Checking the timeline: confirmation and metrics returned to normal matching T18.1, and a draft PR was proposed via Code-Fix after the alert too. Argus catching the P2 flag change itself (when the Investigator missed it) was a solid save. I'm trying to find a "got lucky" moment but nothing really fits — the incident's narrow blast radius (shoppers with past purchases but no purchase this month) feels more like a fault boundary than luck, so I'll leave that section empty.

For still-at-risk, the root issue is that the faulty division logic remains live in the code — re-enabling monthly-spend-feature would likely break account pages again for the same shopper segment. In plain terms: the new monthly spending summary divides by the count of items bought this month, which fails when that count is zero. Technically, average_spend_per_item_this_month divides the month's total by an empty list length for shoppers with no purchases this month, causing the failure.

For action items, I'm separating the gradual rollout idea from automatic error-rate reversion since they address prevention and mitigation differently, plus adding items for linking alerts to on-call paging and refining the investigator's query.

I'm noting the CF-1 test gap is already covered by AI-2's tests, so no new item is needed there. For assumptions, I'm flagging that the empty purchases list explanation comes from Code-Fix's static reading rather than verified execution, and that the timing evidence (errors starting before P2's flag change, resolving after reverting monthly-spend-feature alone) supports isolating that flag as the cause.

Tracing the causal chain: ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code is tied to the monthly-spend-feature flag flipping on, with flag evaluations returning "on" from the first minute onward, ruling out gradual rollout as a factor. The failure rate climbed sharply once this new code path activated, so I'm pulling the before/after error share numbers to quantify that jump.

Checking whether any earlier change could explain this -- the record shows no change before P1, and no relevant deploys, so this is the sole candidate cause. Had testing included a shopper with zero purchases that month, the flaw would likely have surfaced before the flag went live, catching it before shoppers were affected.

action_items.item: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, holding each change at a small share of traffic before widening it.
Turn a newly enabled io-shop flag back off automatically when the error rate rises while it is being rolled out.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged.
Make the Investigator's read of production changes return every flag change from the flag provider's history, including changes on other flags.

causal_chain.step: Account pages failed for shoppers. The share of requests that failed rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}.

Account page requests failed because the spend summary code raised ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors began in the onset minute and kept coming until the alert.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. The read of production changes returned no deploys, and all replicas ran one revision.

The flag an-unrelated-feature, switched on at {P2.1}. That was after the division errors had already begun, and turning off monthly-spend-feature by itself brought the service back while an-unrelated-feature stayed on.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}. In the first minute most flag evaluations already returned on, and every evaluation after that did. Before the change, every evaluation returned off.

With the flag on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page started a calculation that likely divides by the number of items a shopper bought this month, so it fails for any shopper who has bought nothing yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has past purchases but none this month. The tests Code-Fix proposes are new.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would likely have failed before the flag was switched on, so the fault would have been found before it reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No staged rollout or automatic guard was seen on the flag change. In its first minute monthly-spend-feature already served most evaluations, and after that it served all of them.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: With a rollout that held the flag at a small share of traffic and turned it off when errors rose, far fewer shoppers would have hit the failing page, and the flag would have been turned off sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: Argus turned monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed {T21.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
Argus read the flag provider's history itself and found the change to an-unrelated-feature, which the Investigator's read of changes had not returned. This let that change be ruled out.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request #385 {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, with two new tests.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged, because the alert was linked to no on-call incident.
The Investigator's read of production changes did not return the switch-on of an-unrelated-feature. Only Argus's separate read of the flag provider's history found it.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total by `len(bought_this_month)`. That list keeps only this month's purchases. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month it is empty, so the division at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The calculation that fails is still in the code behind monthly-spend-feature, so switching that flag back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
